reason: The cited evidence (E3) confirms that LPBF generates residual stresses and defects, but neither E1 nor E3 provides any support for the claimed effects of a secondary remelting pass on homogenization, stress relaxation, or mechanical improvement in AlCrFeNiSi. E2 actually warns that excessive energy density and slow scanning can cause evaporation, balling, and porosity, which directly conflicts with the proposed intervention. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi produces compositional segregation, high residual stresses, and interlayer defects
A secondary lower-energy laser remelting pass can dissolve local compositional gradients and heal micro-defects
The remelting pass reduces residual stress accumulation by alleviating thermal and compositional discontinuities
Reduced segregation and residual stresses lead to improved mechanical properties (strength, ductility)
Real-time thermal monitoring can optimize remelting parameters to avoid overheating
